segments.text: "Welcome to Robotics Roundup, your daily dose of the latest news from the world of robotics.
August 19th, 2026.
Today, we're tracking a trio of exciting developments that showcase the cutting-edge innovation happening across the globe.
From China's humanoid hardware dominance, to the rise of AI-powered robots in European factories, and breakthroughs in soft robotics that could revolutionize repair and adaptation.
Stay tuned for all 13 of this week's top stories."
From Humanoids Daily, "Unitree Soars Over 600% in Shanghai IPO, Cements China’s Lead in Humanoid Hardware."
Unitree Robotics made its highly anticipated public listing on the Shanghai STAR Market, with its shares skyrocketing by as much as 629%.
The company's strong vertical integration is evident, as 86% of its bill of materials are produced in-house, resulting in margins of approximately 60%.
This achievement demonstrates Unitree's ability to manage its production and supply chain efficiently, a key factor in its rapid growth.
The company's partnership with AI developer DeepSeek to develop embodied intelligence models is also noteworthy, as it aims to address the industry's software bottlenecks.
This strategic collaboration further solidifies Unitree's position as a leader in humanoid robotics.
The public listing marks a significant milestone in China's push to dominate the humanoid robotics market, contrasting with recent US import bans targeting Chinese robotics companies.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Hexagon starts training AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler factories".
Hexagon Robotics and Schaeffler have announced a significant milestone in their collaboration, with the commencement of training for AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler's Humanoid Gym in Germany.

The AEON robots will learn new industrial capabilities by imitating and repeating tasks, with a focus on refining and validating robot policies through representative manufacturing applications from Schaeffler's factories.
This training environment provides a dedicated industrial setting, allowing AEON to build expertise and expand its use cases on the factory floor.
The initiative is expected to support the industrial deployment of AEON and further broaden its application in manufacturing settings.
From Robotics & Automation News, "VUB leads European project teaching soft robots to sense, repair and adapt."
VUB is leading a four-year European research project, RESSORT, aimed at developing soft robots capable of sensing, repairing and adapting.
The project has successfully combined breakthrough technologies, including self-healing materials, variable-stiffness structures, affordable tactile sensors, and artificial intelligence.

By integrating these advanced technologies, researchers have made significant progress in creating soft robots that can learn from their environment, adapt to new situations, and perform tasks more efficiently.
The goal of RESSORT is to make soft robots more sustainable, reliable, and suitable for real-world applications in healthcare, the food industry, and industrial inspection.
The project's findings demonstrate the potential for soft robots to improve efficiency and effectiveness in these fields.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Scientists combine EIT and pneumatic sensing for humanoid robot skin".
Researchers have developed a hybrid robotic skin that combines electrical impedance tomography and pneumatic pressure sensing to improve force detection across large areas of a humanoid robot.
The system uses EIT to determine where contact occurs, while four sealed pneumatic pads provide an estimate of the force being applied.
The hybrid sensing method allows for reduced sensitivity variation, resulting in a 43% decrease compared to EIT alone.
This innovative approach enables more accurate and reliable force detection, enhancing the overall performance of humanoid robots in various applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Faraday Future’s RoboShare takes first paid robot rental order".

Faraday Future Intelligent Electric has announced its support for AIxC Holdings' orderly exit from its digital asset treasury strategy, as the latter will focus on physical AI and robot sharing and rental.
AIxC's robot-sharing and rental platform, RoboShare, completed its first paid commercial order, generating initial revenue for the platform.
The platform's first customer is DU$TY, a Los Angeles-based artist and rapper, and the first paid robot rental order was facilitated through this platform.
RoboShare's success demonstrates the growing demand for robot sharing and rental services, which will likely continue to expand as the technology advances.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS Keeps Evolving via Physical AI SIG".

ROS is undergoing a significant evolution, driven by the collaboration between OSRA and its Special Interest Group on Physical AI, aimed at leveraging ROS's strengths with complementary tools for Physical AI to address the rapid emergence of new tools for robotics.

This effort has resulted in the publication of a blog post detailing the SIG PAI's roadmap and ways for community involvement, outlining the integration of new tools for Physical AI into ROS's existing capabilities.
The SIG PAI has established a framework for community engagement, encouraging users to share their experiences and provide feedback on the evolving ROS framework.
The SIG PAI's work will facilitate a seamless transition of ROS to incorporate both its current strengths and emerging tools for Physical AI.

This development is significant for the AI and robotics industry, as ROS continues to expand its capabilities, ensuring a strong foundation for future innovation and collaboration in the field of Physical AI.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: How robots are learning to navigate the building site"
, this story highlights the development of autonomous robots that can navigate construction sites without relying on GPS, using Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) technology.

Researchers have been working on creating robots that can build a map of the environment using cameras or Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors, combining localization and mapping to create a living map that adapts to the changing site.

SLAM technology has the potential to improve safety, productivity, and error reduction on construction sites, but it is not a straightforward replacement for current methods and is subject to challenges such as airborne dust, physical debris, and integration with existing site management software.
The research demonstrates a promising approach to enabling robots to navigate complex environments on their own.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Rodriguez launches Movotrak ‘seventh axis’ for cobots".
Rodriguez has introduced the Movotrak Cobot Transfer Unit, a system that enables a cobot to move between multiple workstations and extend its operating range to 10 meters.
This innovation allows a single cobot to perform tasks at different positions along a production line, increasing robot utilisation and reducing repositioning requirements.
The CTU features integrated collision detection, which detects collisions while the carriage is moving and automatically stops its motion.
The system can be installed horizontally or mounted on a wall or ceiling, making it suitable for applications such as machine tending and inspection.
This development marks a significant advancement in cobot technology, paving the way for more efficient and flexible automation solutions.
From Robotics & Automation News, "A3 and Mahoning County expand access to free robotics training in Ohio through $500,000 workforce grant."
A3 and Mahoning County Career & Technical Center have secured a $499,000 workforce grant to provide no-cost robotics and automation training to Ohio residents.
The grant will support approximately 3,000 individual course enrollments through June 30, 2027, and is part of Ohio's Individual Microcredential Assistance Program.
The training program, available through the A3 website, will cover topics such as industrial robotics, robot safety, and mobile robot safety.
By expanding access to free robotics training, this initiative aims to equip Ohio residents with the skills needed to succeed in the industry.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Drones With Claws Perch on Arctic Icebergs,"

researchers have developed a drone called Ice Dart, which features spiny feet and shock-absorbing legs that allow it to perch on steep, slippery icebergs in the Arctic, enabling long-term monitoring of glaciers and drifting icebergs.

The development of Ice Dart was accomplished through a combination of robotics and materials science expertise, with the team leveraging 3D printing to create the drone's unique foot structure and testing its capabilities in controlled Arctic environments.
The drone's design enables it to withstand the harsh Arctic conditions, providing valuable insights into the region's climate and ecosystem.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Autonomous drones and the future of war in an AI-driven world | Letter"

, it has been reported that autonomous drones are already being used in warfare, resulting in the killing of civilians and combatants without distinction, highlighting the need for humans to regain control over AI systems.
According to Dr.

Darren Mann, a military surgeon, the lack of transparency in AI decision-making poses a significant risk to humanity, and experts argue that humans must be able to check and audit the decisions made by autonomous systems.
The letter suggests that this is crucial to prevent rogue AI, and Dr.
Mann's proposal emphasizes the need for a more transparent and accountable approach to AI development.
From Humanoids Daily, "Galbot Teases ET1 Bipedal Humanoid Ahead of WRC 2026 Debut".

Galbot has unveiled a CGI teaser showcasing its ET1, a fully bipedal humanoid robot, in preparation for its debut at the WRC 2026 in Beijing, marking a significant architectural pivot from the company's commercial G1 platform.

The ET1's dynamic athletic capabilities were showcased, building on Galbot's LATENT athletic framework, a research initiative that aimed to teach robots athletic tennis skills from fragmented motion capture data, resulting in a successful tennis demonstration.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Warehouse robotics company Brightpick expands partnership with Dr. Max Group."
Brightpick, a provider of AI-powered warehouse automation, is expanding its partnership with Dr.

Max Group, Europe's largest pharmacy chain, to deploy an additional 44 Autopicker autonomous mobile robots across three facilities in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, bringing the total number of deployed robots to 74 units.
The deployment is expected to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual picking labor by 95%, while also increasing warehouse capacity and eliminating picking errors.
The new robots will be deployed across two new projects, both of which are scheduled for completion in the second half of this year.
This partnership expansion highlights Brightpick's growing presence in the European warehouse automation market.
"Robo-tastic, folks!
That's all for today's robotic rendezvous - we're thrilled to have you along for the ride!
Thanks for tuning in, and we hope you're as electrified as Unitree's IPO - see you bright-eyed and bushy-circuits tomorrow!"
